title: Choose which work order gets the lines, or a new one, before drafting
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit' and 'Work orders - Create & Edit', on the build under test; ShopCoach is enabled and the shop has at least one labor type.
  2. A completed inspection with at least one Monitor or Not OK finding, run on a work order. Seed it:
  3. ↳ Open a work order for a customer and asset (Work Orders > New, pick the customer/unit).
  4. ↳ Start an inspection from a template that has a checkbox field; mark one field Not OK and one Monitor.
  5. ↳ Complete and sign the inspection so it is in its read-only completed view.
  6. ↳ For eligibility: have one inspection whose run-on work order is Estimate/Approved/In Progress/Review, and one whose work order is Complete/Invoiced/Paid/Declined (or already invoiced).
custom_steps:
1. Open the completed inspection and press the build action; read the destination menu before any drafting starts.
2. On the eligible-work-order inspection, confirm the run-on work order is offered (by number and status).
3. On the ineligible-work-order inspection, confirm a new work order is created without asking, for the same customer and asset.
4. Confirm an ineligible destination keeps its place in the menu and states why.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Building lines requires ShopCoach; without it the completed inspection offers only the report and a link to its work order, and no build action.
  • The target is chosen before any drafting starts: the work order the inspection was run on, or a new work order.
  • The run-on work order is offered only while it is an eligible build target (status Estimate, Approved, In Progress or Review).
  • When the run-on work order is not eligible (Complete, Invoiced, Paid, Declined, or an invoice already exists), a new work order is created without asking.
  • A new work order is created for the same customer and asset as the run-on work order, using their current values.
  • The destination is chosen from a menu on the build action itself, listing this work order (by number and status) and a new one seeded with the customer and unit, each going straight to drafting.
  • A destination that cannot take lines keeps its place in the menu and says why, rather than silently disappearing.
  • The build action looks the same everywhere: ShopCoach purple with the AI badge, labelled Build lines, with a chevron where it opens the destination menu.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9100 (S2 — Turn findings into work order lines); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S2; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R0: “Building lines requires ShopCoach. Without it the completed inspection offers the report and a link to its work order, and no build action at all”
  • S2-R3: “The user will choose the target before any drafting starts: the work order the inspection was run on, or a new work order”
  • S2-R4: “The system will offer the work order the inspection was run on only while that work order is an eligible build target. Eligible means Estimate, Approved, In Progress or Review. This document does not describe a work order as open or closed: the platform carries several competing definitions of open, and this rule names its own predicate rather than joining them”
  • S2-R5: “When the work order the inspection was run on is not an eligible build target, the system will create a new work order without asking. It is ineligible when its status is Complete, Invoiced, Paid or Declined, or when an invoice already exists. Declined counts as ineligible because lines added to a refused order would revive work the customer turned down”
  • S2-R6: “A new work order will be created for the same customer and asset as the work order the inspection was run on, using their current values”
  • S2-R14: “The destination will be chosen from a menu on the build action itself rather than from a dialog raised before it. The menu lists this work order — by number and status — and a new one seeded with the customer and unit. Either target goes straight to the drafting”
  • S2-R15: “A destination that cannot take lines will keep its place in the menu and say why. A destination that silently stops being offered reads as a fault”
  • S2-R16: “The build action will have one appearance wherever it is met — the ShopCoach purple with the AI badge, labelled Build lines, with a chevron where it opens the destination menu”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.
